one_line: Minister-turned-king of Odisha who overthrew the last Suryavamsi Gajapati heirs and founded the Bhoi dynasty in the mid-16th century.

appearance.age_look: Early 40s, lean but sturdy build, height slightly above average with the bearing of a seasoned court minister and field commander.
appearance.face: Oval face with a straight nose, medium-brown Odia complexion, sharp dark eyes under slightly arched brows, a neatly trimmed short moustache and light stubble along the jaw, a small tilak on the forehead, default expression calm and calculating with a hint of stern resolve.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair oiled and pulled back into a small low knot at the back of the head, front kept smooth with no loose bangs, wrapped at the base with a narrow maroon cloth band; no crown, only a simple narrow golden forehead band (patta) resting above the tilak.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate mid-16th century eastern Indian court-warrior attire: an unbleached off-white cotton angarakha-style upper garment reaching mid-thigh, fastening diagonally across the chest with a subtle wrap and side tie, long fitted sleeves; over this a sleeveless quilted cotton war-vest in muted mustard-gold with fine vertical stitching suggesting padding but no fantasy armor; a deep indigo cotton dhoti wrapped tightly and secured at the waist, pleats drawn between the legs for easy movement, ending at the ankles; around his waist a broad maroon cotton kamarband with a darker red edge, its ends hanging slightly at one side; simple leather sandals on the feet; jewellery kept modest—thin gold bangles on each wrist, a discreet gold ring on the right hand, and small round gold ear-studs; a light cream cotton uttariya (shawl) with a narrow red border draped from the left shoulder under the right arm and back over the left forearm, giving him both courtly and martial presence.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved single-edged talwar with a plain steel blade, a simple brass hilt and disc pommel, carried in a dark brown leather scabbard with minimal brass fittings, usually worn at his left hip through the maroon kamarband, his right hand often resting lightly on the hilt to show the tension between ministerial duty and his decisive usurpation.

ref_desc: Govinda Vidyadhara is a lean early-forties Odia man with an oval face, short moustache, oiled black hair tied in a low knot with a maroon band and a simple golden forehead band, wearing an off-white angarakha, mustard-gold quilted vest, deep indigo dhoti, maroon waist sash, cream shawl, modest gold jewellery and leather sandals, carrying a plain-hilted talwar in a dark brown scabbard at his left hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw an anime-style full-body model sheet of Govinda Vidyadhara: a dignified, lean early-forties Odia man with an oval face, medium-brown complexion, sharp dark eyes, small tilak, and a neatly trimmed short moustache with light jaw stubble, expression calm and calculating. His thick black hair is oiled and pulled back into a small low knot at the back of his head, secured with a narrow maroon cloth band, and he wears a thin golden forehead band above the tilak, with no elaborate crown. Dress him in mid-16th-century eastern Indian court-warrior clothing: an unbleached off-white cotton angarakha-style upper garment reaching mid-thigh with long fitted sleeves and a diagonal wrap closure, covered by a sleeveless mustard-gold quilted cotton war-vest with fine vertical stitching; a deep indigo cotton dhoti wrapped tightly and pleated between the legs to the ankles; a broad maroon cotton waist sash (kamarband) tied at the front with its ends hanging slightly at one side; and a light cream cotton shawl with a narrow red border draped from his left shoulder under the right arm and back over the left forearm. Add simple leather sandals, thin gold bangles, small round gold ear-studs and a single gold ring. At his left hip, through the maroon sash, place his signature weapon: a slightly curved single-edged talwar in a dark brown leather scabbard with a plain brass hilt and disc pommel, his right hand resting lightly on the hilt. Use a palette of off-white, mustard-gold, deep indigo, maroon and dark brown, and show him from head to toe in a clear, consistent design suitable for repeated redrawing.
